        "content": "For task-0cb18964, a small connected object of a distinct color in an otherwise noisy grid is a stencil. Keep the stencil unchanged. Search every translation of its occupied-cell mask within the large grid; whenever every stencil cell lands on background zero, color those matching zero cells with the stencil color. Output is the union of all matches. Do not require the empty cells inside the stencil bounding box to be zero. Demonstrations: color 3 multi-cell pattern, color 5 vertical 3-cell pattern, and color 1 L triomino all behave this way. In the test the 1 stencil mask was {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2)}; matches at (6,8),(10,16),(13,15), recolored with 1. First wrong attempt left grid untouched; then correct by enumerating all translations and recoloring union. Confirmed again on task-0cb18964: stencil was an 8-colored L triomino with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}. Enumerate placements against the original grid (all three cells must be 0), collect union, then recolor union 8. Overlapping placements are allowed; their union can form larger connected regions. Do not scan mutably and let earlier recolorings suppress later matches. A one-pass mutable scan was wrong; original-grid eligibility and union was correct. Preserve stencil. Confirmed again on task-0cb18964: stencil was an 8-colored L triomino with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)}.
